subtopics.title: The Vital Statistics — Birth, Death and Natural Increase

questions.question: The crude birth rate is measured as:
options: Live births per thousand people in a population per year
Births per woman over her lifetime
Births per hundred families per month
The total number of births in a country

questions.question: South Africa has a birth rate of about 19 per thousand and a death rate of about 9 per thousand. Its rate of natural increase is:
options: 28 per thousand, or 2,8% a year
About 10 per thousand, or roughly 1% a year
9 per thousand, or 0,9% a year
19 per thousand, or 1,9% a year

questions.question: Germany's death rate is higher than Kenya's mainly because:
options: German healthcare is worse than Kenyan healthcare
Kenya records deaths less accurately
Germany has a much older population, and elderly people die at higher rates
Germany has a higher birth rate

questions.question: The rate of natural increase deliberately EXCLUDES:
options: Deaths of infants
Births to young mothers
Deaths of the elderly
Migration into and out of the country

subtopics.title: Fertility, Infant Mortality and Life Expectancy

questions.question: Replacement-level fertility is about 2,1 children per woman because:
options: Governments set it as a legal target
Two children replace the parents, and the extra fraction covers children who do not survive to adulthood
Every family needs at least two workers
It is the world average fertility rate

questions.question: Infant mortality is considered the most sensitive single indicator of development because:
options: It is the easiest rate to count
It only depends on the number of hospitals
Babies are counted twice in the census
Keeping babies alive requires clean water, nutrition, vaccination, clinics and educated mothers all working together

questions.question: South Africa's life expectancy fell to around 53 years in the early 2000s and then rose by more than a decade. The recovery was driven mainly by:
options: A fall in the birth rate
Emigration of older people
The mass rollout of antiretroviral treatment for HIV
An increase in the fertility rate

questions.question: A country has low life expectancy. The correct interpretation is:
options: The average is dragged down, often heavily by infant deaths — many adults may still reach old age
Nobody in the country grows old
The country must have a low birth rate
Its population must be shrinking

questions.question: On a population pyramid, males and females are shown:
options: Males on the right bars, females on the left bars
Mixed together in single bars
Males at the bottom, females at the top
Males on the left bars, females on the right bars, in five-year age cohorts from youngest at the bottom

questions.question: A notch — one cohort clearly smaller than its neighbours — usually points to:
options: A past war, famine or epidemic that killed people or suppressed births in those years
A printing error in the graph
A baby boom in that generation
Heavy immigration of that age group

questions.question: The dependency ratio compares:
options: Males against females
The young and aged dependants against the economically active aged 15 to 64
Births against deaths
Urban population against rural population

questions.question: Sides of a pyramid that rise almost vertically show that:
options: The birth rate is extremely high
Many people die young
Most people survive from each age group into the next, into old age
The country has more males than females

subtopics.title: Three Pyramid Shapes and South Africa's Own

questions.question: An expansive pyramid — wide base, quickly tapering sides — indicates:
options: Low birth rate and an ageing population
High birth rate, high mortality, rapid growth and low life expectancy
Zero population growth
A population dominated by pensioners

questions.question: A constrictive pyramid has a base NARROWER than the bars above it. This means:
options: The death rate among children is very high
The census failed to count children
Many young adults have emigrated
Fertility has fallen below replacement — the population is ageing and will shrink

questions.question: Which trio correctly matches shape to country?
options: Expansive — Japan; stationary — Niger; constrictive — Sweden
Expansive — Germany; stationary — Mozambique; constrictive — the USA
Expansive — Niger; stationary — Sweden or the USA; constrictive — Japan or Germany
Expansive — Italy; stationary — the DRC; constrictive — Mozambique

questions.question: South Africa's pyramid is best described as:
options: Transitional — a still fairly wide but no longer widening base, a bulge of young adults, and a taper marked by the Aids years
Perfectly stationary with vertical sides
Strongly constrictive like Japan's
A pure triangle like Niger's

questions.question: Japan's fertility rate is about 1,3 children per woman. In the long run its population will:
options: Grow slowly
Stay exactly the same
Shrink, because fertility is below the replacement level of 2,1
Double every 50 years

questions.question: A country where half the babies die in infancy and the survivors live to 80 has a life expectancy of about 40. This shows that:
options: Nobody in that country reaches old age
Life expectancy is an average that infant deaths drag down hard
The calculation must be wrong
The country has a low birth rate

questions.question: The lesson's warning about judging countries from indicators is:
options: Only life expectancy matters
Indicators from poor countries cannot be trusted
Death rates are always lower in rich countries
Never judge on one number alone — ask who is in the population and use several indicators together

subtopics.title: The Pyramid as a Family Photograph

questions.question: In the family-photograph picture of a pyramid, a strangely SHORT row compared with its neighbours means:
options: Something reduced that generation — a war, epidemic or famine when they were born or young
That age group refused to be photographed
A baby boom happened in those years
The country stopped keeping records

questions.question: In the oldest rows of most pyramids, the female bars are longer than the male bars because:
options: More girls are born than boys
Old men are not counted in the census
Women outlive men almost everywhere in the world
Women immigrate more than men

questions.question: The three blocks used for the dependency question are:
options: Babies, teenagers and adults
Under-15s and over-64s as dependants, with the 15-to-64 group supporting both
Men, women and children
Rural, urban and suburban residents

subtopics.title: Wide Base, Narrow Base — What the Shape Tells You

questions.question: Population momentum in an expansive pyramid means:
options: The population stops growing as soon as fertility falls
Old people migrate back to rural areas
The pyramid keeps the same shape forever
Today's huge child cohorts become tomorrow's parents, so growth continues for decades even after fertility falls

questions.question: Fast-forwarding a constrictive stack thirty years gives:
options: A wide base and narrow top
Many pensioners resting on few workers — which is why such governments encourage child-bearing
A perfectly even tower
Rapid population growth

questions.question: South Africa's fertility has fallen since the 1960s from about:
options: 6 children per woman to about 2,3
3 children per woman to about 2,8
2,1 children per woman to about 1,3
8 children per woman to about 5

questions.question: South Africa's current demographic window of opportunity exists because:
options: The country has more pensioners than workers
The birth rate is rising quickly
An unusually large share of the population is of working age relative to dependants
Most of the population is under 15
